scope: Georgia · civil and criminal procedure (separately scoped references)

esig_regulation.term: Law on Electronic Documents and Electronic Trust Services
esig_regulation.basis: Article 3(1): a qualified electronic signature has the same legal effect as a handwritten signature. Article 3(2): a qualified electronic seal allows the integrity and origin of an electronic document to be verified, and these are deemed genuine unless proved otherwise.

data_access_basis.term: Law on Personal Data Protection, Article 5
data_access_basis.basis: Processing is admissible only on a ground listed in Article 5(1), such as consent, a contract, a legal provision or another listed ground. Supervision is exercised by the State Audit Office (Article 39).

timestamp_recognition.term: Law on Electronic Documents and Electronic Trust Services, Article 7
timestamp_recognition.basis: Article 7(1): qualified time stamps carry a presumption of accuracy of the time and date and of the integrity of the related data. Article 7(2) sets the requirements, including an accurate time source linked to Universal Time.

evidence_rules.basis: No evidence has a predetermined weight. The court evaluates evidence by inner conviction after a comprehensive, full and impartial examination.

Written evidence includes acts, documents and correspondence with information on important circumstances. An electronic document under the Law on Electronic Documents and Electronic Trust Services has evidentiary value.

Evidence obtained through a substantial violation of the Code is inadmissible if it worsens the accused's position. Evidence is also inadmissible where a reasonable doubt that it was replaced or its properties changed has not been refuted.
Evidence is evaluated for relevance, admissibility and trustworthiness, has no predetermined force, and a conviction requires agreed evidence beyond reasonable doubt.
